title: Why Can't Anyone Answer Questions About the Business? — Garrett Galow, WorkOS
talk_summary: WorkOS built an internal 'Studio' agent (Opus + tool integrations to Snowflake/Linear/Notion) that answers business questions and generates reusable declarative widgets. The transferable engineering is their reliability pattern: pre-flight checks, just-in-time tool context injection, distrust of model priors, and mandatory query validation before hardcoding.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of preloading all tool docs into the system prompt, they inject a long schema/usage context block only at the moment the agent decides to invoke that specific tool.
takeaways.evidence_quote: at the time it decides to invoke a tool, that's when we inject context around how to use the tool

takeaways.what_they_do: The agent runs pre-flight checks (tools connected? enough context?) and asks clarifying questions before choosing tools, rather than immediately executing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we make it run a lot of pre-flight checks ... If not, ask clarifying questions

takeaways.what_they_do: Before hardcoding a generated query into a widget, the agent executes it and confirms it returns data, catching syntactically valid but useless outputs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have it always run the query and validate that it gets data back

takeaways.technique: Distrust model priors, force primary sources
takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly instruct the model to distrust its trained knowledge of the product and look up current docs/primary sources instead.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we tell it to like no no no, go for primary sources, look up data in our docs

takeaways.technique: Compile agent output into declarative code, then stop using the LLM
takeaways.what_they_do: The agent generates a widget as JavaScript (UI + API calls + query); afterward refreshes run the code directly with no LLM in the loop, only re-invoking the model when the widget is edited.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the LLM's not involved once the widget is developed

takeaways.technique: Same eval suite in staging and production
takeaways.what_they_do: They run evals in both staging and production instances and treat them identically so dev experience matches teammate experience.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we use evals uh in both our staging and production instances. We treat all of that the same
